description: Agent Events: submit an event’s ticketing record with the announced ticketing terms: the record with the event, the currency, each tier with its id, name, price and quantity, and the refund terms (whether refunds are allowed, the last refund day and the refund fee as a percent); the terms with the event, the currency, each announced tier with its name, price and quantity, and the announced refund terms. The signed report gives the record and the terms, each announced tier paired with a record tier by name, every announced tier missing from the record named, each pair’s price and quantity on each side and the refund terms on each side, and counts them, and names a discrepant record: an announced tier missing from the record, another currency, a higher price or fewer tickets than announced, and refunds withheld, ended earlier or charged more than the announced terms state; then an unannounced tier, a lower price, more tickets, more generous refund terms and another event name, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. A price or quantity on one side only, refund terms the record leaves unstated, or terms that name no tiers leaves the record unverified. Tiers pair by their words with plurals folded, prices compare to the cent in one currency and refund fees to the hundredth of a percent. This reads an event’s ticketing record against what was announced: wever_pricing-tier-check reads one pricing page’s plan tiers, billing periods, limits and features against plan terms text, while the ticket check reads an event’s ticket tiers, quantities on sale and refund terms against the announced ticketing terms and reads no plan or subscription pricing; wever_refund-eligibility-check reads one purchase against a refund policy and decides a claim, while the ticket check decides no refund claim; and wever_sports-plan-trip assembles a trip with event tickets and the cheapest-ticket lookup finds a listed ticket price for an attendee, while the ticket check reads the organizer’s own ticketing records and sells or refunds nothing. Verdict event_ticket_discrepant, event_ticket_partial, event_ticket_unverified or event_ticket_consistent. POST /api/event-ticket-check. Reads the event records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between documents only: it never books a venue, registers or invites anyone, sells or refunds a ticket, publishes an announcement, or judges whether an event should happen, was well run, or was worth attending, only whether its records agree with each other and with what was announced, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Events reads an organized event’s records for consistency between documents: an event brief, a published agenda, speaker confirmations, a registration list, a venue arrangement, a ticketing record, a public announcement and a post-event report, each against the requirements, plan, lineup, capacity and eligibility terms, brief, announced terms, schedule or records it should agree with. Beside it, the Standing jobs rail tools such as wever_schedule-create register, list, report on and cancel recurring jobs and keep state, and wever_meeting-brief states one meeting’s decisions and action items from its notes, while this family keeps no state, registers nothing, runs nothing and reads the records in the call against each other and against what was announced. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-events-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-events/.
